## Overview

SIGNAL is a statistical method to detect spatially variable genes (SVGs) in
single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics and to classify each one by the
source of its spatial variation.

![](figures/SIGNAL_Fig1_overview.svg){width=100%}

For each gene, SIGNAL fits a multi-kernel variance component model,

$$
\mathbf y \sim N\!\left(\mathbf 0,\;
\sigma^2_c \mathbf K_{\text{cell type}} +
\sigma^2_s \mathbf K_{\text{spatial}} +
\sigma^2_{ct} \mathbf K_{\text{cell type} \times \text{spatial}} +
\sigma^2_0 \mathbf I\right),
$$

with a cell-type kernel, a spatial kernel and their interaction. The variance
components are estimated by MINQUE, and SIGNAL runs

* an **overall test** of $\sigma^2_c = \sigma^2_s = \sigma^2_{ct} = 0$, which
  detects any spatial or cell-type variation (utSVGs), and
* three **component tests**, which separate its source:
  * **cell type** ($\sigma^2_c$): expression differs between cell types (cSVG);
  * **spatial** ($\sigma^2_s$): expression varies over space for all cell
    types (sSVG);
  * **cell-type-specific spatial** ($\sigma^2_{ct}$): the spatial pattern
    differs between cell types (ctSVG).

The test statistics follow mixtures of chi-square distributions, whose tail
probabilities are computed with Davies' method. Results are combined over a
panel of 11 spatial kernels (Gaussian, Matérn and thin-plate spline) with the
Cauchy combination test. A second-stage test finds the cell types that carry
each ctSVG pattern: a spatial test within each cell type's cells for
single-cell data, and a test of one cell type's interaction kernel for
spot-level data.

## What SIGNAL returns

A table with one row per gene and the four p-values (`p_overall`,
`p_celltype`, `p_spatial`, `p_ctSVG`), and, for selected genes, a
genes $\times$ cell types table of cell-type-specific p-values.

## Tutorials

| Page | Data | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| [Installation](Installation.html) | | Installing SIGNAL on Linux, macOS, Windows and HPC clusters |
| [Getting started](tutorial.html) | Simulated example (in the package) | The full workflow, runs in about a minute |
| [Axolotl brain](Artista.html) | Stereo-seq, 4,410 cells, cell-type labels | Single-cell data, 11 spatial kernels, batches of genes on a cluster |
| [Mouse hypothalamus](Mouse.html) | MERFISH, 5,520 cells, cell-type labels | Single-cell data, a single Gaussian spatial kernel |
| [Mouse hippocampus](Alzheimer.html) | STARmap PLUS, 9,244 cells, cell-type proportions | Spot-level data, large data |

The processed real data used in the tutorials can be downloaded from the
[SIGNAL real data folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-j6l-KBT9dR_p2RB2RVb_5q9Ig2GdRn3)
on Google Drive.
